subject: Dedicated capacity architecture & proposed offer — Asterion Health
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@asterionhealth.com>, Asterion Procurement <procurement@asterionhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity architecture & proposed offer — Asterion Health

Hi Liam + team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to hear how Asterion is planning to scale inference for chart summarization and real-time triage over the next 18 months. As promised, attaching a concise offer and a sizing workbook with three phased options so you can see trade-offs by latency SLO and monthly committed GPU-hours.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Option A (Conservative): 24 x A100-equivalent min floor, phased to 48 over 9 months. Good for predictable throughput and tight SLA guarantees.
- Option B (Balanced): 16 x min, ramp to 40 over 6 months with burst capacity on demand. Best cost vs latency for expected growth.
- Option C (Light on-commit): 8 x min, step-ramp model with scheduled warm-up windows; lower cost but longer tail latency under peak.

I've included a "cluster-sizing-table.xlsx" with per-model token throughput, seq-length assumptions, and suggested warm pools. Ben reviewed the numbers and offered tweaks for prefix caching and batching that reduce token cost by ~18% in Option B.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm which option aligns with Asterion's procurement comfort and budget band.
2) If legal wants a draft SOW/term sheet, we can push a redlined offer (I attached a working PDF) and loop in our contracts team.
3) Schedule a short follow-up next week to lock ramp dates (I have Q1 slots Wed/Thu).

Attachments: cluster-sizing-table.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_dedicated_offer_v2.pdf (proposal PDF)

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189
Redwood Inference

From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@asterionhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:27:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity architecture & proposed offer — Asterion Health

Thanks Priya — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions before procurement advances: 

1) For Option B, what is the guaranteed p95 latency for a 4096 token sequence when the cluster is at 85% utilization? We need p95 numbers to include in our SLA appendix.
2) On the minimums: is the "min floor" billed as reserved capacity (monthly) or is there an alternative blended billing you can do for the first quarter to smooth onboarding spend?
3) On data residency — all inference stays in our US East VPC — is there anything we need to sign or configure for private deployment?

Also procurement asked if you can add a 60-day activation window (we may need a staged start with financial holdbacks).

If you can send a short one-page SLA appendix and mark up where the activation window would live in the offer, that would help move this along.

Best,
Liam

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity architecture & proposed offer — Asterion Health

Looping in Grace for legal/ops on activation windows and SLA language. Quick answers to Liam's bullets: 

1) p95 latency (Option B): ~220ms token-step median, p95 for 4096-token seq at 85% util — ~1.6s end-to-end per request with our batching profile (we've modeled concurrent chat + batch jobs). I'll include the modeling assumptions.
2) Billing: the min floor is a reserved monthly commitment. We can offer a smoothing credit for Q1 (blended effective rate) that recognizes a staged ramp; can be structured in the term sheet as a ramp credit schedule.
3) Data residency: for Private deployment we operate over a customer VPC peer; no data is persisted to our control plane other than telemetry. We'll add a one-paragraph technical binder to the offer that calls out KMS integration and audit log retention.

I've attached an excerpt SLA appendix and updated the cluster sizing workbook with a suggested 60-day activation holdback schedule in the notes tab. Priya — please review and send to Liam with the attachments.

Attachments referenced: cluster-sizing-table.xlsx (updated)

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Liam — thanks for the questions and the fast turnaround. Attached are the two items requested: a one-page SLA appendix (PDF excerpt included in the offer PDF) and the updated sizing workbook with the 60-day activation holdback schedule called out in the notes. Key points up front: 

- p95 latency (Option B) at 85% util: 1.6s for a 4096 token end-to-end request (modeled assumptions are on tab "PerfModel").
- Billing structure: monthly reserved minimum with a Q1 smoothing credit applied as a line item (see Offer v2, Section 2.3).
- Private deployment items: KMS integration and audit log retention are listed in Section 4; we'll deliver the technical binder during onboarding and can include an addendum in the SOW.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Procurement: review the attached Offer v2 (redwood_dedicated_offer_v2.pdf) and confirm whether the 60-day activation holdback is acceptable — if yes, we'll produce the redlined terms for your legal team.
2) Technical: we'll schedule a 45-minute design session with our private-deploy engineering lead to validate VPC peering and KMS runbook (available Tue/Thu next week).
3) Commercial: Ben and I will prepare a simple run-rate comparison for the three options showing net-effective rate after credits.

I look forward to your confirmation so we can lock dates in the SOW.

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
